transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi, thanks. Well, I came in because... I've been having some trouble with eating lately. It mostly happens after my late shifts at work. I'll stop for food on the way back, but then I just keep going once I get home. 

Like, I'll finish a full takeout meal, and then move on to chips, sweets... really just whatever is in the apartment. And then afterward, I'm just kind of shocked by how much I actually ate.
After these episodes, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain or make up for what you ate, such as vomiting, fasting, or exercising excessively?

Yeah, I do. Um... since my apartment move settled into a routine, it's been happening most weeks. I'll have at least one of those late-night episodes where I eat way past what I meant to. And then to make up for it, I... well, I'll try to fix it by throwing up. Or sometimes I'll just completely skip breakfast the next day, or force myself to go on a really long run to burn it off.
How long has this pattern of binge eating followed by behaviors to compensate been happening?
I'd say it's been going on for... about a year and five months now. It started right around the time I moved into this temporary apartment down near the tourist district.
How much do your weight or body shape affect how you judge yourself as a person?

I mean, it's definitely something I think about. I wouldn't say it completely controls how I see myself, but... yeah, it bothers me. If I feel like I'm gaining weight or looking out of shape, I get pretty down on myself. It just feels like something I should be able to control better, you know? So, it does affect my self-esteem, for sure.
